title: Unbounded ordinary etale compact supports composed with a proper direct image
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $g:Y\to S$ a separated finite-type morphism, where $S$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each morphism $h:T\to B$ in $\{f,g,gf\}$ choose a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,r:\overline T\to B)$ as in [def-asd-compactifiable] and let $Rh_!^c=Rr_*j_!$ be its ordinary unbounded small-etale compact-support functor [def-amb-etale-compact-support], on $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. A refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ of compactifications $c_i=(j_i,r_i)$ means a proper map $u:\overline T_1\to\overline T_2$ over the target with $uj_1=j_2$. The proper-refinement comparison $Rr_{2,*}j_{2,!}\to Rr_{1,*}j_{1,!}$ is obtained by applying $Rr_{2,*}$ to the canonical proper/open comparison $j_{2,!}\to Ru_*j_{1,!}$ and using derived direct-image composition. Specify the proper/open map on a K-injective representative $J$ of an input complex on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]: choose a K-injective resolution $j_{1,!}J\to I$ on $\overline T_1$ and take the morphism represented by $j_{2,!}J\cong u_*j_{1,!}J\to u_*I$, where the first arrow is the proper/open identification of module sheaves restricting to the identity on $T$. These proper-refinement comparisons are isomorphisms on the whole unbounded category; identity refinements give identities, composable refinements give composites, and comparison through a common refinement is independent of that refinement and satisfies the cocycle condition. Thus write $Rh_!$ for the resulting compactification-independent functor. There is a canonical isomorphism of functors
$$
\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!:D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)\longrightarrow D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A).
$$
Here $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ is normalized by the compactification $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$, and $\alpha_{g,f}$ is the compactification composition comparison obtained by interchanging open extension by zero with proper derived direct image. This comparison is natural in the input complex and compatible with the proper-refinement identifications; in particular it is independent of compactification choices. No boundedness or constructibility condition is imposed.

proof.text: Check the geometric and coefficient hypotheses first. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y,S$ are Noetherian, and so is every ambient compactification scheme: its proper structural map is of finite type over its Noetherian target. Properness includes separatedness and finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The separatedness and local finite type of $gf$ follow from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); quasi-compactness follows by taking a finite affine cover of $g^{-1}(W)$ for an affine $W\subset S$ and then finite affine covers of its inverse images under $f$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The compactifications in the statement therefore have exactly the type required by [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. A finite ring is a torsion ring: its additive group has finite exponent. In particular, the unbounded, finite-ring assertion of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] applies; no invertible prime is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F7H, section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification, torsion-ring paragraph; Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, case (b)

proof.text:
Let $u:c_1\to c_2$ be a refinement for $h:T\to B$. Apply [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] to the square with top $j_1:T\hookrightarrow\overline T_1$, bottom $j_2:T\hookrightarrow\overline T_2$, left proper map $1_T$ and right proper map $u$. The square need not be cartesian. Its map, after identifying $R1_{T,*}$ with the identity, is an isomorphism $\gamma_u:j_{2,!}\to Ru_*j_{1,!}$. On a K-injective representative $J$, the cited statement specifies exactly $j_{2,!}J\cong u_*j_{1,!}J\to u_*I$ for a K-injective resolution $j_{1,!}J\to I$; the sheaf identification is the identity on $T$. Thus it is the map specified in the item, not merely an unspecified isomorphism between its source and target. Put $F_c=Rr_*j_!$ and define
$$C_u:F_{c_2}\xrightarrow{Rr_{2,*}\gamma_u}Rr_{2,*}Ru_*j_{1,!}\xrightarrow{\kappa^{-1}}F_{c_1}.$$
Here $r_2u=r_1$ and $\kappa$ is the canonical natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied to the constant-$A$ ringed small etale topoi. Every factor is invertible and natural on the entire unbounded category.

proof.text: For $u:c_1\to c_2$ and $v:c_2\to c_3$, the vertical-pasting and identity assertions of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], with all left proper maps identities, give $\gamma_{vu}=(Rv_*\gamma_u)\gamma_v$ and $\gamma_{1}=1$, with the specified direct-image compositors inserted. Whiskering by the proper structural direct image, as in step 2, gives $C_{vu}=C_uC_v$ and $C_1=1$. The cofilteredness statement [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] supplies both common refinements and equalizers of parallel arrows. For $d\xrightarrow{u_1}c_1$, $d\xrightarrow{u_2}c_2$, set $I_{12}=C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}:F_{c_1}\to F_{c_2}$. For two such choices, first dominate their refinement objects and then equalize the resulting two pairs of arrows to $c_1,c_2$. The equation $C_{vu}=C_uC_v$ makes both expressions equal, since the extra invertible factor from the common dominating object cancels. For three compactifications choose a single dominating object and write all three comparisons this way. Direct cancellation gives $I_{23}I_{12}=C_{u_3}^{-1}C_{u_2}C_{u_2}^{-1}C_{u_1}=I_{13}$. Also $I_{11}=1$ and $I_{21}=I_{12}^{-1}$. These equations prove choice independence and the cocycle condition for the actual maps of step 2, and justify the notation $Rh_!$.

proof.text: Because $f$ is proper, $(1_X,f)$ is a compactification. For an identity open immersion every object of the small etale site factors through the open. The presheaf formula in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] is therefore already the original sheaf, with its original restrictions and maps, so $(1_X)_!=1$ naturally, also degreewise on complexes. The candidate of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] for $(1_X,f)$ is consequently exactly $Rf_*$. The comparisons $I$ of step 3 identify every other $Rf_!^c$ with this candidate. This defines the required normalization $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$; its value at the trivial compactification is the identity by $I_{11}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0F7H, section-derived-lower-shriek-compactification, definition applied to the trivial compactification

proof.text:
Construct the composition comparison on compatible models. Fix $d=(i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y,s:\overline Y\to S)$ for $g$ and any compactification of $gf$. By [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], choose $e=(a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to\overline Y)$ compactifying $if$. Its statement supplies $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $q:V\to Y$ and $j:X\hookrightarrow V$ with $pb=iq$, $bj=a$, $qj=f$, and all the required proper/open properties. The square with horizontal maps $b,i$ has the unbounded interchange isomorphism $\Gamma:i_!Rq_*\to Rp_*b_!$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange]. Whisker it by $Rs_*$ and $j_!$. The canonical direct-image composition of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the degreewise open composition of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] give the natural isomorphism
$$D_{d,e}: (Rs_*i_!)(Rq_*j_!)\xrightarrow{Rs_*\Gamma j_!}Rs_*Rp_*b_!j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(sp)_*a_!.$$
These are exactly the candidates of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] for $g,f,gf$. Use step 4 and $I_{(1_X,f),(j,q)}$ to identify the second input candidate with $Rf_*$. Finally use the comparisons of step 3 for $g$ and $gf$. This gives $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ with precisely the proper/open composition normalization in the statement.

proof.text:
Verify compatibility with refinement of a whole tower. Any two towers have a common refining tower by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], so consider a tower indexed by $1$ mapping to one indexed by $2$. The cited statement supplies proper maps $u:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y_2$, $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$, $w:V_1\to V_2$ with $ui_1=i_2$, $va_1=a_2$, $wj_1=j_2$, $vb_1=b_2w$, $p_2v=up_1$, $q_2w=q_1$, and $s_2u=s_1$. For this calculation abbreviate $I_i=i_{i!}$, $J_i=j_{i!}$, $B_i=b_{i!}$, $P_i=Rp_{i*}$, $L_i=Rq_{i*}$, $M=Ru_*$, $H=Rv_*$ and $H'=Rw_*$. Write $\gamma_A:J_2\to H'J_1$, $\gamma_D:I_2\to MI_1$, $\gamma_E:B_2J_2\to HB_1J_1$, $\gamma_F:B_2H'\to HB_1$ for the interchange maps of the four refinement squares, and $\gamma_B:I_2L_2\to P_2B_2$, $\gamma_C:I_1L_1\to P_1B_1$ for the two model squares. Every square has proper verticals and open horizontals; the refinement squares need not be cartesian. The two pasting laws in [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] say
$$\gamma_E=(\gamma_FJ_1)(B_2\gamma_A),\qquad(M\gamma_C)(\gamma_DL_1)=(P_2\gamma_F)(\gamma_BH').$$
Naturality of $\gamma_B$ at $\gamma_A$ says
$$(P_2B_2\gamma_A)(\gamma_BJ_2)=(\gamma_BH'J_1)(I_2L_2\gamma_A).$$
Substitute these equalities to obtain
$$(P_2\gamma_E)(\gamma_BJ_2)=(M\gamma_CJ_1)(\gamma_DL_1J_1)(I_2L_2\gamma_A).$$
Composition is read right to left. Applying $Rs_{2,*}$ and inserting the canonical direct-image compositors of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the open compositors of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] identifies this with
$$C_{gf}D_2=D_1(C_gF_{f,1})(F_{g,2}C_f).$$
Here $F_{f,i}=L_iJ_i$, $F_{g,i}=Rs_{i,*}I_i$, $D_i=D_{d_i,e_i}$, and $C_f,C_g,C_{gf}$ are precisely the comparisons from model $2$ to model $1$ constructed in step 2. Thus the composition map intertwines all three specified refinement comparisons. Compare two towers through their common refining tower and cancel invertible comparisons using the cocycle in step 3. The normalized map of step 5 is independent of all tower and compactification choices. All its factors are natural transformations on unbounded derived categories, so naturality in the input complex is also established; no boundedness or constructibility hypothesis entered the argument.
